purpose: Fleet harness pre-registration. The fleet-mode law, harness, arms and scoring were frozen before any run on the held-out seeds.
selection: Fleet-mode constants were selected by random search (70 + 90 configurations) on development scenarios (seeds 101-104 of every vessel). Selection rule, fixed before selection: lowest mean energy relative to HPA 0.7 + Cluster Autoscaler among configurations that beat HPA 0.7 + Karpenter-lite on both energy and node reversals in every vessel, with time healthy >= 0.99 (web, multi, batch) and work completed within 0.2% of the baseline. Eight configurations met the rule. The selected configuration is record 55 of SEARCH_70.jsonl (script search_70.py). search_90.py explored an additional up_band parameter; no selected configuration uses it and it has been removed from the governor, so search_90.py documents the exploration but no longer runs against the current code.
gate_selection: The equation (2) gate was extended to capacity additions (push_add). Balanced (0.0098) and wear-first (0.0035) thresholds were chosen on development seeds 101-104 as the 75th and 50th percentiles of the push measured on the fleet plant; energy-first keeps the original setting. All three were frozen before the held-out run from seed 600000; the earlier held-out run from seed 500000 was evaluated with the energy-first setting only and is superseded.

families.elastic: web, multi, batch, gpu: powering nodes off is permitted
families.always_on: gpu_always_on: powering nodes off is not permitted; every arm may only park idle nodes (Ready, 25% of idle power, wake in one tick) and cap power

idle_power_path: omni_fleet_park: the energy-first fleet law with capacity reductions executed as parking instead of power-off.
families_note: The always-on family, the idle-power arm and separate park accounting were added and frozen before the held-out run from seed 700000, which supersedes the run from seed 600000.
